public_payload.normalized_proposition: More data center debt makes both data centers and debt costlier, and stopping new financing would pressure all existing debt.
conditions: if new data center debt financing stops

statement.excerpt: This is the Doom Loop: the more data center debt that gets raised, the more expensive both the data centers and the debt become, and the only way of fixing the problem is to stop financing new data center debt, except once that happens, everybody will ask whether the data center buildout has stalled, which will in turn create pressure on all of the debt that’s already been issued.

from_speaker: the more data center debt that gets raised
the more expensive both the data centers and the debt become
the only way of fixing the problem is to stop financing new data center debt
create pressure on all of the debt that’s already been issued
our_interpretation: The plain reading asserts a causal feedback mechanism, an exclusive remedy, and a further consequence if new financing stops.
Pressure on existing debt means worsening credit conditions, such as falling prices, rising spreads or greater default risk.
Issuance and costs moving together would not alone establish that issuance caused the increases.
This is assessed as a causal claim. The financing-stop clause remains an unobserved contingency unless a qualifying halt is documented.
No company-specific monetary amount is asserted, so metric_scope is null.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence identifies increased issuance as a cause of both financing and development cost increases, establishes why stopping issuance is necessary, and documents or credibly identifies broad existing-debt stress caused by a financing halt.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible evidence breaks a necessary link, demonstrates another effective remedy while financing continues, or shows that a qualifying halt does not exert the asserted broad pressure.
